title: synoreclaim scan --detach result v1
description: The one JSON line scan --detach prints and flushes before it returns (SPEC 5.3). completion complete: job_id names a queued job; failed (exit 1): a target did not resolve, see errors; busy (exit 4): every filesystem is locked by another writer, see errors[].holder. No job is kept unless job_id is set. resume --detach and cleanup apply --detach print the same line (SPEC 5.11, 5.7); a refused cleanup apply prints the cleanup-apply failure document instead. NAS-wide admission refuses a second queued/running scan with exit 4, completion busy, outcome scan_in_progress and running_job_id; job_id remains null and run is empty.

launcher.description: self: synoreclaim started the job in a new session; none: the caller runs it, e.g. under a service manager.

run.description: The argv that runs the queued job in the foreground (scan --job-id ID --state-dir DIR; cleanup apply --yes --json ... --job-id ID ... -- PLAN); empty when no job was queued.

result.description: jobs/<job_id>/result.json, where the run leaves its whole document (scan, or cleanup-apply); null when no job was queued.

log.description: jobs/<job_id>/output.log, the stdout and stderr of the job's own process with launcher self; null otherwise.

outcome.description: scan_in_progress: a scan already occupies NAS-wide admission; no new job is queued. joined (exit 0, rootfs.report only): a walk of / is already queued or running; job_id and running_job_id name it, run is empty and nothing new starts.

running_job_id.description: The existing queued/running job to follow when outcome is set.
